ledger.x: 6 April 1814: the Bourbons are restored in France.
Treaty of Paris (1814) page: France retained 'Saarbrücken, Saarlouis, Landau, the County of Montbéliard, part of Savoy with Annecy and Chambéry'.
20 November 1815: the Second Treaty of Paris takes 'Landau and the Saarlouis exclave, which had been French since 1697' (Treaty of Paris (1815) page, which names no recipient).
20 November 1815: 'The former duchy of Bouillon, annexed to France in 1795' is ceded (Treaty of Paris (1815) page).
Saarlouis page: 'With the Treaty of Paris in 1815, Saarlouis (and the whole region later known as the Saargebiet) became Prussian.'
20 November 1815: six communes of the Pays de Gex go to Geneva.

20 November 1815, Second Treaty of Paris: 'parts of France were to be occupied by up to 150,000 soldiers for five years, with France covering the cost', 'in the eastern border territories of France, from the English Channel to the border with Switzerland'.
ledger.cp: Seventh Coalition army of occupation (austrian-empire, kingdom-of-prussia, russian-empire and British forces)

ledger.x: 1818: 'the foreign troops withdrew from France in 1818' (Treaty of Paris (1815) page); the Restoration page agrees ('Until 1818').
ledger.cp: Seventh Coalition army of occupation (austrian-empire, kingdom-of-prussia, russian-empire and British forces)

ledger.x: 7 April 1823: 'the "100,000 Sons of Saint Louis" under the Duke of Angoulême entered Spain without opposition'; Cádiz surrendered on 30 September and the army left 'an occupying force of 45,000 men under the command of Bourmont'.
1828: 'Spain was then progressively evacuated, but the French withdrawal was fully completed only in 1828.'
14 June 1830: French troops land at Sidi Ferruch.
5 July 1830: Algiers falls.
9 August 1830: the House of Orléans replaces the Bourbons as Louis Philippe becomes King of the French.

15 November 1832: the Siege of Antwerp page's infobox dates the operation '15 November - 23 December 1832' and says the marshal 'returned with his army to Belgium November 15, 1832, when he laid siege to Antwerp'.
23 December 1832: the Antwerp citadel capitulates.
January 1836: Clauzel occupies Tlemcen.
May 1837: the Treaty of Tafna.
1838: France establishes a protectorate over the coast of Gabon.
Late 1839: the war with Abdelkader resumes.
13 March 1844: 'the Tahitian populace began an armed resistance on 13 March 1844'; the first battle the page names is Mahaena, 17 April 1844.
17 December 1846: 'the capture of Fort Fautaua' ended the guerrilla conflict; 'In February 1847, Queen Pōmare IV returned from her exile and acquiesced to rule under the protectorate.'
December 1847: Abdelkader surrenders.
1848: the Gabon protectorate passes to the Second Republic.
24 February 1848: the July Monarchy falls to the February Revolution.

wars.name: Hundred Days
wars.outcome: 'Napoleon, on 20 March 1815, returned to Paris from Elba'; 'On 8 July 1815 the kingdom was restored'.

wars.name: French intervention in Spain (Hundred Thousand Sons of Saint Louis)
wars.outcome: 'On 7 April, the "100,000 Sons of Saint Louis" under the Duke of Angoulême entered Spain without opposition'; Fort Trocadero was assaulted on 31 August, 'On 30 September Cádiz surrendered', 'The French army fired its last shots in Spain at the start of…

wars.name: French conquest of Algeria
wars.outcome: 'French victory' (infobox 1830-1847): landing 14 June 1830, Algiers 5 July 1830, annexation of the occupied areas 22 June 1834, Abdelkader's surrender in December 1847.

wars.name: Belgian Revolution (French intervention at Antwerp)
wars.outcome: William I's invasion of Belgium 'on 2 August 1831' brought French help; 'Marshal Gérard assisted the young Belgian monarchy with 70,000 men, taking back the citadel of Antwerp, which capitulated on 23 December 1832'.

wars.name: Franco-Tahitian War
wars.outcome: 'French victory' (infobox 1844-1847): armed resistance from 13 March 1844, Mahaena 17 April 1844, Fort Fautaua captured 17 December 1846; 'In February 1847, Queen Pōmare IV returned from her exile and acquiesced to rule under the protectorate.'

certainty.note: Metropolitan frontiers are treaty lines (the 1814 treaty, then 1 January 1790 after 20 November 1815); the overseas cells (Senegal, Guiana, the Antilles, the Gabon coast) are approximate and should be drawn soft.
